title: EECS Undergraduate Newsletter 04-05 - EECS at Berkeley
content: EECS Undergraduate Newsletter 04-05 - EECS at Berkeley Categories Newsletter View Open Faculty Positions Undergraduate EECS Newsletter - Spring 2024 - Friday, April 05, 2024 Faculty Advising will occur Monday, April 15th – Friday, April 26th for all students declared in the EECS or CS majors. We hope you’re excited about this opportunity to connect with faculty and hear about their experiences and advice. Faculty Advising is primarily intended for discussion of course, graduate school, and industry questions. Although no longer required, you are encouraged to attend Faculty Advising, as it is an important opportunity to connect with faculty. Questions about policy and/or specific degree requirements should continue to be directed to staff advisors. What to Bring to Faculty Advising Questions! These can be related to course selection, graduate school, and industry. Faculty members are not expected to answer questions about department policies, petitions, or degree requirements. For more information on Faculty Advising see our FAQ or email at faculty-advising@eecs.berkeley.edu ━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━ BIO Spring 2024 Emergency Aid Fund for F-1 and J-1 International Undergraduate Students The BIO Emergency Aid Fund is a living expenses award intended for those in need of short-term aid due to unforeseen circumstances such as geopolitical events, natural disasters or other extenuating circumstances. If you are or know of an F-1 or J-1 international undergraduate student facing severe financial hardship due to such situations, please schedule a time to speak with a BIO advisor . ━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━ Updates on the Transfer of the Computer Science Major to CDSS The College of Computing, Data Science, and Society (CDSS) has been established and three undergraduate majors have transferred from the College of Letters & Science (L&S) to CDSS. The three undergraduate programs in CDSS are: Computer Science, Data Science, and Statistics. April 7th at 1-4pm. There will be food! Bring your friends! Please RSVP at https://forms.gle/xHC4HajJYR5SG2M56 ━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━ Innovation Day Showcase We are thrilled to announce the upcoming Innovation Day (IG: @innovationday.berkeley) on April 21st , a vibrant celebration of invention and creativity showcasing Berkeley’s innovators. This day-long event is designed to be a melting pot of ideas, talents and passions from across our campus, bringing together entrepreneurs, designers, engineers, creatives, alumni, and investors. Ever wish you had an event to showcase your creations to the Berkeley community? Curious to see what other students are working on? This is your chance! Along with multi-disciplinary student showcasers, we have a day packed with speakers from various fields of innovation and ample opportunities to form genuine connections with driven students, accomplished alumni, and prospective investors. It's a unique opportunity to bring campus innovators together, to learn from one another, and meet other students, alumni, and investors. Apply now to showcase at Innovation Day (deadline is 4.7). If you want to come to the event, please reserve your free student ticket here. Don’t miss out on this opportunity to celebrate creativity, explore new ideas, and catapult your vision into a reality. Join us and let’s make Innovation Day a memorable event! ━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━ Machine Learning + Systems Research Panel Looking to land research opportunities for the summer? Or want to understand more about different research areas in CS? HKN has invited ML and systems researchers from Berkeley's own labs to answer all questions research. Our guests will be sharing what they are working on, the process of developing an idea to having papers accepted into top conferences, getting into top grad schools, what a career in research looks like, and how you can join a research lab too! We look forward to seeing you! Time: Monday, 4/8/24, 6-8 PM Location: The Woz, Soda 430 ━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━ Biotech + Artificial Intelligence Symposium Interested in Biotech, Tech, startups, and healthcare consulting? The Bio-Business Initiative is hosting our annual Biotech Symposium on Monday, April 8th from 8-10 pm . Join us and learn from five industry professionals from NVIDIA, Databricks, 310.ai , SynBioBeta, Pinnacle Healthcare Consulting, and more! Our speakers have unique experiences in the Bay Area's science and business industries and can provide excellent advice for those interested in exploring academia, research, or cutting-edge industry opportunities. The event will include a speaker panel session, followed by Q&A and networking. 5 speakers will join us for the event and 3 of them have Tech and AI backgrounds. The speakers with the Tech / Biotech background are: Kooshiar Azimian , a former Machine Learning Engineer at Facebook, is now the founder of 310.ai , a platform dedicated to biomolecule design. Mehrzad Samadi, founder of the scalable genomics analysis software Parabricks (acquired by NVIDIA), currently serves as a Senior Engineering Manager at NVIDIA, focusing on GenAI. Reza Zadeh , an adjunct professor at Stanford and a key member of the founding team of Databricks, will share his experiences in helping to launch the company. RSVP : https://docs.google.com/forms/d/e/1FAIpQLSdmp0d2kYvJcAfQOpYu-Pu75Jgf3n-KLw7RpUyBR6qgBVxP2Q/viewform When: April 8, 2024 @ 8-10 pm Where: Genetics and Plant Biology Room 100 ━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━ L&S Advising Peers Program Looking for a great opportunity to join a dynamic, equity-minded Peer Advising Team? Do you want to develop transferable skills in advising, communications, and participate in equity-focused outreach & engagement events? You're in luck! L&S Peer Adviser Applications are now open for the 2024-2025 academic year. We are seeking students in the College of Letters & Science who will bring diverse backgrounds, identities, and experiences to the peer advising role, and support the L&S Advising mission to provide compassionate support and guidance for students as they navigate their UC Berkeley experience. The priority deadline for applications is April 8 . Pay is $18+/hour or academic credit. Weekly hours can range from 6 - 20. This event will take place on April 10th, 2024, from 12-4 pm at the Pauley Ballroom in the ASUC Student Union: Martin Luther King Jr. Building . This fair is designed for last-minute recruiting and immediate hires, offering a valuable opportunity for students to connect with leading employers across various industries. Check out our list of participating employers . ━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━ Undergraduate EECS Town Hall We invite you to attend the Undergraduate EECS Town Hall, taking place on Thursday, 04/11/2024 4-5 PM at Wozniak Lounge. Co-hosted by the EECS department and HKN, the town hall provides an exclusive Q&A session where students have the opportunity to engage directly with faculty members (including Professors John Denero, Ana Arias, Joey Gonzales, Anant Sahai, and the EECS department chairs). This event provides a platform for undergraduates to discover how EECS/CS undergraduate students can benefit from existing resources, understand the financial state of the department, and explore the newly established College of CDSS and its relationship with EECS/CS. We also invite you to join us in discussions about the incoming hardware-focused ECE major, course offerings, and the future of EECS 16A/B. Students will be given the opportunity to ask pertinent questions and gain insights into various aspects of the EECS program, such as: concerns regarding course enrollment, departmental strategies to improve the educational experience, pathways to research, preparation for graduate school, emerging trends in various fields of EECS, attributes of successful students, and making the most of their undergraduate education at Berkeley. Please note that while we aim to cover a wide range of topics, we kindly request that attendees refrain from asking questions related to the union. Your understanding and cooperation in maintaining the focus on educational and departmental matters are greatly appreciated. ━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━ M.E.T. Innovation Academy (M.E.T. ia ) Summer 2024 Program The M.E.T. Program will be hosting our summer program for high school students for our second year, and we are looking for six UC Berkeley students to be Teaching Assistants (TA’s) for the M.E.T. ia program. Description : The Berkeley M.E.T. Innovation Academy (M.E.T. ia) is a hands-on summer program for rising high school juniors and seniors interested in being at the forefront of tech and entrepreneurship. M.E.T. ia students will get real-world experience solving business and tech challenges and interface with world-renowned corporations and organizations, and will interact with successful entrepreneurs from the heart of Silicon Valley as well as Berkeley M.E.T. student entrepreneurs. Work Hours : Hourly rate: $21.00/hour Mid-May through early-June: You’ll be ramping up, course planning, and being trained, working closely with the Faculty Director. Expect to work ~10-20 hours per week through early-June. June 10 - June 14; June 17-21; July 1-5. Expect to work full time (40 hrs/week) Program hours are 8am-5pm; some evenings or weekends may be required. The program ends in early-July but follow up work will be required through mid-July Main Responsibilities : Help refine the curriculum by working with faculty to develop curricular content and assignments, and/or research into 60-90 minute hands-on activities and/or group projects Create a facilitator guide, coordinate logistics, develop supply lists, lesson plans, etc. as needed for each days activities Support class sessions and lead activities Conduct application exercises Mentor student teams on their projects Attend off site excursions and support students as needed Skills & Qualifications : Must be able to start work in mid-May to begin developing curriculum (can be remote for this portion). Must be available to work fulltime on campus June 10 - July 5 40 hrs / week to help prepare for and deliver the program (on campus - no remote option). Demonstrated interest in working with high school students in STEM and entrepreneurship focused camps. Strong desire to teach, lead and develop curriculum. Highly organized and able to handle multiple projects simultaneously with an eye toward prioritizing work to meet deadlines. Ability to thrive in an open-office environment and interact with all levels of organization. Strong verbal + written communication and interpersonal skills. High level of comfort working with people from diverse cultures. General computer and administrative skills. Comfortable with asking questions, pursuing answers, and operating with minimal guidance to move work forward. Mastery of programs such as Word/Excel, Google Suite, Adobe Suite, Canva, Slack. HTML/CSS skills are a plus. Experience working in campus maker spaces, research labs, etc. is a plus. Some lifting required. Aware of and practices the UC Berkeley Principles of Community and leads with a DEIBJ inclusivity mindset. To apply: Submit your resume and cover letter (showing your demonstrated interest/experience in working with high school students in a STEM and entrepreneurship focused camp) to met@berkeley.edu by April 12, 2024. Please use the subject line: “M.E.T. ia Teaching Assistant Position Application.” ━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━ PhD in Statistics (+ related fields) Panel The UC Berkeley Statistics Graduate Student Association is hosting a panel on PhD programs. The panel will consist of Ph.D. students from a variety of STEM departments (statistics, biostatistics, math, computational precision health). Come learn more about what graduate school is like, the admissions process, and the difference between PhD programs of various disciplines. There will be food. We especially encourage early-stage and underrepresented students to attend! When: Monday, April 15, 2024 at 6:00-7:00 pm Where: Evans 1011 Action item: Please RSVP here if you plan to attend. Please try to RSVP by Friday, April 12. ━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━ SLP Peer Academic Coach The SLC Strategic Learning Program is excited to announce that we are hiring Peer Academic Coaches for Fall 2024! We are looking for undergraduate students who are passionate about the learning process and committed to supporting their peers in achieving their academic goals. By becoming a Peer Academic Coach, students can not only assist their fellow learners but also refine their own learning strategies, deepen their understanding of the neuroscience of learning, and broaden their professional skill sets. Students can see the full job card and access the application at bit.ly/Apply-SLP . We will be reviewing candidates on a rolling basis, with the first deadline coming up on April 15 . ━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━ A Peak Into Engineering Interview Join us to learn how to advocate yourself as a qualified candidate for engineering/cs interviews! When: April 17th, 4-5pm Where: Hearst Memorial Mining Building Room 290 RSVP: https://tinyurl.com/eopstemxbmc ━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━ Berkeley Analytics Lab Showcase Date: Tuesday, April 23, 2024 Time: 11:00 a.m. - 2:00 p.m. Location: Mudd Hall RSVP here by April 9 to secure your place at the forefront of analytics innovation. Join us for the Berkeley Analytics Lab Showcase from 12 pm to 2pm on Tuesday, April 23, 2024 , where students will showcase data-driven solutions developed in the 2024 Analytics Lab Spring semester course. From posters to app demos and interactive features, the Berkeley Analytics Lab Showcase is a culmination of hands-on analysis and research conducted by Berkeley Analytics students who have spent the semester utilizing cutting-edge analytical methods and quantitative tools to tackle real-world business and industry challenges. This showcase will explore the transformative power of analytics across an array of industries. From sports and entertainment to the forefront of fashion, finance, generative AI, healthcare, and beyond. We can answer questions about professors, majors, student organizations, and campus life in general. Along with academic advisors, we can assist you in tailoring your experience in the CS major. Topics regarding financial wellness, include creating a spending plan, understanding credit score and credit report, managing credit cards, saving and banking, moving out of the dorms, and eating on a budget. Workshop schedule : click here ! ━━━━━━━━━━━━━ Basic Needs Center team is committed to fostering belonging and justice on the UC Berkeley campus through a robust model that includes both short-term emergency relief and long-term support services addressing students’ basic needs. All enrolled students including undergraduate, graduate, international and undocumented students are eligible for Basic Needs Center resources and services. We define basic needs as an ecosystem that at the core includes food security , housing security , and financial stability . We recognize that basic needs must be approached in a holistic manner, and may include health/medical care, technology, and transportation needs in addition to our core ecosystem.
